title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-10-14
body:
Weekly update (2026-10-14) — Serving Runtime: kernel work, KV cache, batching

Attendees / Standup notes:
- Priya Nair (owner): overall sync, rollout plan for kernel v2.1.
- Ethan Cole: batching SLA tests, latency regressions investigation.
- Sofia Martinez: KV cache metrics, eviction policy changes.
- Liam Chen: CI GPU infra flakiness, repro + fix for assembly kernel failure on A100s.
- Quick shoutouts: Ming and Carla for the kernel microbench harness and new p95 collector.

High-level summary:
- Kernel v2.1 branch is feature-complete for attention-fusion and row-major GEMM path. Microbenchmarks show 8–12% token throughput improvement on long-seq workloads (seq_len 2048) vs v2.0.
- KV cache improvements merged to main: deterministic eviction + async persist for prefix cache. Cache hit rate increased from 71% to 86% on the conversational workload in internal canary.
- Batching: dynamic batch sizing landed for text-generation route; throughput up ~18% during peak while keeping 95th latency within SLO for 90% of requests. Some regressions remain for short, low-latency traffic — follow-up flagged.

Kernel work (owner: Priya, review by eng-serving-runtime):
- Merged PR #4321: attention operator fusion + kernel dispatch table changes. Notes: this reduces attention kernel launch overhead by ~30% for tiny heads (h=8).
- Ongoing: add autotuning pass to pick row-major vs col-major GEMM per model layer during warmup. Prototype shows wins on 8-bit quantized GPT-style models.
- Blocker: occasional assembly kernel crash on A100 reported in CI (flaky repro). Root cause narrowed to misaligned L2 prefetch in the custom load routine. Liam is working on a patch; ETA Wed next week.
- Canary plan: staged rollout to 10% of hosted inference traffic for kernel v2.1. Canary checks: p50 and p95 latency, correctness fuzz tests, and sampled token-level diff against v2.0. If stable for 48h, expand to 50%.

KV cache (owner: Sofia):
- Deployed deterministic LRU-with-segment eviction and async checkpointing for long-lived sessions. This avoids the previous interleaving bug that caused stale KV reads under GC pressure (JIRA-INF-789).
- Metrics: cache_hit_rate increased to 86% (from 71%), average eviction latency reduced from 12ms -> 4ms. Memory growth under synthetic long-conversation tests capped as expected.
- Observability: added per-tenant prefix-hit-rate dashboard; alert if hit_rate drops >15% vs baseline.
- Follow-ups: evaluate bloom-filter style pre-check to short-circuit cache lookups for tiny prefixes (task INF-807).

Batching (owner: Ethan):
- Dynamic batcher merged (PR #4334). It uses recent request inter-arrival histograms to decide per-model batch windows, with a soft cap on latency.
- Results from dedicated canary: throughput +18% during 11am–1pm peak for search-heavy workload; cost per token down ~9% for that route.
- Regression: for sub-100-token requests with strict 50ms p95 requirement, some tails increased by 8–10ms. Root cause: batching window sometimes coalesces a tiny request behind a slow-to-assemble KV fetch.
- Mitigation: added small-request fast-path bypass to short-circuit batching for <20-token requests and cold KV. Initial tests show p95 latency back within SLO for these classes.

Reliability / SRE notes (owner: Liam):
- CI flakiness: repro for assembly kernel crash in GPU CI; isolated to specific CUDA 12.3 driver + A100 microcode combo. Temporary mitigation: skip affected CI matrix cell and add hardware filter. Long-term: patch to kernel loader underway.
- Rollback hooks: canary deploys have automatic fallback to v2.0 with traffic-split policy if error rate > 0.5% or token-level diffs exceed threshold.

Metrics snapshot (canary region, last 48h):
- Kernel v2.1: token throughput +10% (avg), p95 latency +1.5% (within SLO).
- KV cache: hit_rate 86%, avg eviction latency 4ms, memory growth stable.
- Batching: route X throughput +18%, cost/token -9%, short-request p95 initially +9ms then returned to SLO with fast-path.

Decisions made:
- Proceed with staged canary for kernel v2.1 (10% -> 50% -> full) conditioned on 48h stability windows and token-diff checks.
- Enable dynamic batcher for text-generation routes in hosted-prod for non-low-latency tiers.
- Backport deterministic eviction fix to 2.0 branch for private deployments on older stacks (JIRA-INF-802).

Action items / Owners (next 7 days):
- Liam: finish assembly kernel patch and push hotfix for CUDA 12.3 incompatibility (ETA: 2026-10-21).
- Priya: finalize autotuner integration and run full regression suite on representative models (ETA: 2026-10-20).
- Sofia: instrument bloom-filter pre-check experiment in canary (INF-807) and report by next update.
- Ethan: finish short-request fast-path telemetry and run 48h A/B to confirm tail reductions (ETA: 2026-10-19).
- Ops: update canary runbook with new rollback thresholds for token-diff checks (owner: Carla).

Open questions / risks:
- Does autotuner introduce non-determinism that could affect token-level diffs? Need to ensure warmup decisions are logged and reproducible.
- Hardware matrix is getting more fragmented (driver/microcode combos) — consider gating nightlies by hardware profile to catch regressions earlier.

Notes / links:
- Kernel PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4321
- Batcher PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4334
- KV cache design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/serving-runtime-kv-cache-design
- Jira: JIRA-INF-789 (KV eviction bug), JIRA-INF-802 (backport to 2.0)

Next sync: Weekly cadence as usual — Thu 10:00am PT.

Quick personal notes (informal):
- Left TODO in PR #4321 to add more unit tests for tiny-head attention paths — low priority but helpful for long-term stability.
- Reminder: schedule post-canary retro to capture lessons on batching window heuristics.

End of update.
